highlights.title: Verdict runs right / misleading / wrong: 81 / 28 / 2 -> 88 / 23 / 0 -> 110 / 1 / 0 -> 110 / 1 / 0.
highlights.detail: Checks 229 / 41 / 2 -> 252 / 24 / 0 -> 254 / 1 / 0 -> 254 / 1 / 0. Campaign 1's misleading classes were fixed in campaign 2, campaign 2's (packet_loss false positives from hole punching, relay_fallback_failed on a slow relay path) in campaign 3; what remains in campaigns 3 and 4 is one sampling miss of 1 % loss in 3 runs.

highlights.title: Outcomes: final direct / relay / failed 49 / 42 / 2 -> 51 / 42 / 0 -> 51 / 42 / 0 -> 51 / 42 / 0; lost connections 2 -> 0 -> 0 -> 0.
highlights.detail: The direct/relay outcome of every scenario is the same in all four campaigns; the two failures of campaign 1 were the lossy link's connections closed after request timeouts.

highlights.title: Lossy link across the campaigns:
highlights.detail: campaign 1: connection closed in 2/3, verdict 'through a relay', loss hint 0/3, concurrency 1/3; campaign 2: survives 3/3, relay_fallback_failed 2/3, loss hint 2/3, concurrency 0/3; campaign 3: survives, relay fallback ok 13/13, loss hint 11/13, concurrency 11/13, one upload failed by a race (1/13); campaign 4: healthy/exit 0 13/13, relay fallback ok 13/13, loss hint 9/13 (sampling), concurrency 13/13 (2 restarts), no transfer failure.

highlights.title: Concurrency on fast paths:
highlights.detail: campaigns 1-3 reported the 200 ms tick (156 Mbps in every lab direct run, 74/78 relayed); campaign 4 measures 185-252 Mbps lab direct, 74-81 relayed, 213-330 real-world direct.

highlights.title: Measurements stable:
highlights.detail: lab RTT 40.4 / 80.6 ms and throughput ~123 / ~35 Mbps direct / relayed in all four campaigns; real-world RTT and throughput vary with the ~34 / ~37.5 ms route clusters, and a few runs per campaign (1 / 0 / 2 / 3) hit a slow Hetzner -> lab direction; 418.5 / 418.4 / 418.7 / 418.3 MB through the real relay with no drops.
